description: Game-genre taxonomy + MECHANIC (how each is played), read + grounded from the on-disk Wikipedia. The GENUS says what category a game is; the MECHANIC (the differentia the construction grammar extracts and the agent KEEPS) says how it is PLAYED — and that is what lets the jabberwock ASSESS the game in front of it. The NAVIGATION/MOVEMENT mechanic (platformer: move the avatar between points; maze: from an entrance to a goal) is what a game like ls20 instantiates — an avatar moved through a space to reach a goal-cell.

concepts.name: action_game
concepts.mechanic: emphasises physical challenges — hand-eye coordination and reaction time (real-time reflexes)
concepts.comment: genre read+grounded from Wikipedia; the mechanic is the kept differentia.

concepts.name: strategy_video_game
concepts.mechanic: strategic / tactical planning and decision-making — indirect control of multiple units, management of limited resources (turn- or real-time, not reflexes)

concepts.name: adventure_game
concepts.mechanic: the player is a protagonist in an interactive story, driven by exploration and/or puzzle-solving

concepts.name: tile_matching_video_game
concepts.mechanic: manipulate tiles to make them disappear according to a matching criterion

concepts.name: racing_video_game
concepts.mechanic: the player participates in a racing competition

concepts.name: platformer
concepts.mechanic: MOVE THE PLAYER CHARACTER (avatar) between points in an environment — the navigation/movement mechanic; a game where an avatar is moved through a space to reach a target instantiates this

concepts.name: maze_game
concepts.mechanic: navigate a maze of paths from an ENTRANCE TO A GOAL — reach the goal by moving through the navigable space, avoiding walls

concepts.name: tetris
concepts.mechanic: arrange FALLING tetromino pieces (four connected blocks) to complete and clear horizontal lines
concepts.comment: the PUZZLE GAME, NOT the Georgian monetary unit 'tetri' — the earlier homonym sense-slip, corrected by reading the game lead.
